title: Project defense: explain decisions and make an independent change
goal: Present reproducible applied work, answer from your data and finish assessment with honest boundaries.

prerequisites.text: 1c-enterprise.a 7; A1–A2: separate infobase, catalogs, references and documents; synthetic data only.

sections.title: From a familiar situation to a checkable question
paragraphs: A defense explains your work and transfers it to a new condition. Explain why the restored copy became 420 while the original remained 400, then show the particular document. The author’s technical protocol does not answer for you or award an instructor grade.

sections.title: Where to act
paragraphs: Use only your synthetic service. Main 440/225/215 and new independent 400/420 are different sets and evidence; do not force them to agree. Preserve the original, DT/CF, attempts and previous work; restore only into a new empty target. Nexus stores a note and independent A/Pprogress; it neither executes external 1C nor awards instructor grades.

sections.title: A defense explains decisions
paragraphs: Show model, workflows, checks and recovery rather than reciting definitions. Explain field types, references versus names and rejected-write behavior. Review questions concern the actual deliverable. A local system may preserve answers as self-report but cannot call that an independent defense.

Defend your actual infobase: locate customer / service / request / filter, justify types and explain rejection. Trace one report row back to documents. Definitions without your own demonstration are insufficient. Prepare a 5–7-minute presentation and an artifact list.

sections.title: Reason before acting
paragraphs: Use your own installed 1C result and independent controls.
Identify the infobase, list and particular record separately. A command, visible text and saved state are different things.

sections.title: How to carry out the worked example
paragraphs: Follow the route in your prepared own copy. This is the worked example; the new task below uses different data. Compare each expectation with your actual reread.
Step 1. Prepare model, one report row, refusal and recovery demonstration with versions / paths / keys. Expected: Explanation traces to data.
Step 2. Predict and execute one changed condition, then rerun old checks while retaining the pre-defense version. Expected: Skill transfer demonstrated.
Step 3. Complete theory variant, four tasks and one project. Record actual status, own artifact references and limits. Expected: Assessment parts distinguished and preserved.

Step 4. Retain source / DT / notes / answers / provenance. If continuing toP, create a new work item without transferring A marks. Expected: Reproducible result with retained attempts and independent progress.

sections.title: A transfer change checks understanding
paragraphs: Select another customer in the existing filter or change one valid document in a new copy. Keep the absent period filter as a separate requirement. Predict the result, create a copy and change it without a solved walkthrough. Then repeat prior workflows. Explaining the consequences of a changed condition demonstrates understanding better than replaying a memorized click sequence.

Make a control change in another copy: a different customer filter, a valid extra document or an optional field. Predict before acting and repeat old cases afterward. Retain the pre-defense version, changed copy and answers rather than replaying one memorized route.

paragraphs: Do the author’s green technical checks mean that a learner defended a project and completed track P?

reveal.title: Check the reasoning
paragraphs: No. These are different claims. Your selected variant and project need your own files, answers and observations. Theory, four practical works, the project and independent assessment are distinct; A progress does not transfer to P.

sections.title: Transition to P is optional
paragraphs: An applied graduate operates the system and performs foundational configuration within scope. Professional P adds algorithms, modules, queries and engineering verification. Shared concepts help, but A completion does not automatically complete P topics. Transition creates a new work copy with provenance rather than transferring unrelated competency credit.

Open this direction’s Nexus final assessment and complete your theory variant, four practical tasks and selected project rubric. Keep actual files/DT separately: links/self-reports do not upload or automatically verify execution. Retain previous attempts.

sections.title: Check the explanation’s boundary
paragraphs: Reading does not replace the practical capstone.
Demonstrate actual records, independent checks and recovery separately.

sections.title: The final package remains learner work
paragraphs: Preserve the pre-defense version, changed copy, answers and transfer-check results. Do not erase attempts to beautify the record. Declare templates and assistance without claiming unverified independent authorship. Instructor grading and certification belong to a separate process that local self-checking does not replace.

Programming is an optional next direction. Shared knowledge helps but A completion does not mark P topics complete. State templates and Akronikl/other assistance as provenance. Teacher certification / authorship verification requires a separate process, not an imitation by the local candidate.

sections.title: A new independent task
paragraphs: Prepare a 5–7-minute account of your 400/420 work: model, one report row’s path, two refusals, actual restoration and the 20-minute difference. Choose one more valid new condition in a separate copy, such as another customer in the existing filter, predicting before generation. Keep absent period/status support as a requirement. In final work record actual statuses of your variant’s theory, four practical works and selected project, your attachments and NOT RUN. Do not automatically transfer A grades to P or call self-reporting an independent defense.
Record a prediction first. After your own attempt reveal the reference and compare the selected record as well as its number.
